day_materials.title: 綜合測驗短文：City Rooftop Gardens（克漏字，空格以 {{11}}–{{15}} 標記）
day_materials.content:
In many crowded cities, empty rooftops are quietly being turned into green gardens. At first, this idea sounds like a luxury that only wealthy neighborhoods can {{11}}. However, research suggests that rooftop gardens bring practical benefits to almost everyone. During hot summers, a thick layer of plants keeps the top floor cooler, which {{12}} the amount of electricity used for air conditioning. The same plants also soak up rainwater that would otherwise rush into the streets and overload the drains.

Beyond these physical effects, green roofs change how people feel about where they live. Office workers who once ate lunch at their desks now climb the stairs to sit among vegetables and flowers. {{13}}, several companies report that their employees seem calmer and more focused after a short break outdoors. A few schools have even moved certain science lessons to the roof, where students measure temperature and observe insects instead of only reading about them in textbooks.

Of course, building a rooftop garden is not {{14}}. The roof must be strong enough to hold the wet soil, and someone has to water the plants regularly. Yet as more cities face rising summer temperatures, these green spaces are no longer seen as mere decoration. Instead, they are becoming a practical tool that helps a community {{15}} a warmer future.
day_materials.translation_zh: 在許多擁擠的城市，閒置的屋頂正悄悄被改造成綠色花園。起初這聽起來像只有富裕社區才負擔得起的奢侈，但研究顯示屋頂花園幾乎為每個人帶來實際好處：夏天厚厚一層植物讓頂樓更涼、減少冷氣耗電，也吸收原本會沖進街道、讓排水溝負荷過重的雨水。綠屋頂還改變人們對居住地的感受，員工爬上頂樓在蔬果花草間休息，公司回報員工更平靜專注，有些學校甚至把自然課搬到屋頂。當然，蓋屋頂花園並不輕鬆，屋頂要夠堅固、要有人固定澆水；但隨著城市面臨升溫，這些綠地已不只是裝飾，而是幫助社區面對更炎熱未來的實用工具。

question_slots.stem: Although the new medicine cannot completely cure the disease, it can significantly ______ the patient’s pain within a few hours.
question_slots.explanation: 【句意中譯】雖然這款新藥無法完全治癒疾病，卻能在數小時內大幅______病人的疼痛。→【正解C】前有讓步連接詞 Although 與 significantly，語意需與「無法根治」相對、朝正面走：diminish（減少、減輕）與 pain 搭配，正好表「減輕疼痛」。→【辨析】(A) amplify 是「放大、增強」，會變成加重疼痛，與 significantly 減痛語意相反；(B) preserve「保存、維持」等於維持疼痛，不通；(D) inherit「繼承」與 pain 無搭配。→【評析】考點為近義／反義動詞辨析與 Although 讓步語境判讀，屬中等難度。

day_materials.title:
文意選填短文：The Science of Forgetting（空格 {{21}}–{{25}}；詞庫見下）
詞庫 Word Bank：(A) failure  (B) importance  (C) discard  (D) recognize  (E) connections  (F) preserve  (G) obvious  (H) reminder　※每格填一字、字不重複，字庫中有 3 字不會用到。
day_materials.content:
Most people think of forgetting as a sign of a weak or aging brain. When we cannot recall a name or a password, we quickly blame ourselves for being careless. Yet scientists now argue that forgetting is not simply a {{21}} of memory. Instead, it is an active and useful process that the brain performs on purpose. In recent years, this new view has slowly moved from a handful of laboratories into ordinary conversations about how the mind really works.

Every single day, our senses take in an enormous amount of information. If the brain stored every detail with equal {{22}}, we would soon be buried under useless facts—the color of a stranger’s shirt, the exact words of an old advertisement, the temperature of last Tuesday afternoon. To keep the mind clear, the brain constantly decides which memories to keep and which ones to {{23}}. Forgetting, in this view, is a kind of mental cleaning that removes what no longer matters.

This process also helps us think more flexibly. When old and trivial details fade away, the brain can more easily {{24}} the general patterns hidden in our experience. A doctor, for example, does not need to remember every patient she has ever met; she needs the shared symptoms that help her name a disease. By letting go of single events, the mind grows better at forming useful {{25}} between them.

Of course, forgetting can go too far. Illness and injury may erase memories that we truly need, and that kind of loss is painful. But for a healthy brain, everyday forgetting is not a failure at all. It is a sign that the mind is working exactly as it should, quietly sorting the daily flood of experience into something we can use. Seen in this light, a forgotten detail is not a hole in our knowledge but the small price we pay for a mind that stays quick, clear, and ready for what truly matters.
day_materials.translation_zh: 多數人把遺忘當成腦力衰弱或老化的象徵，記不起名字或密碼就怪自己粗心。但科學家主張，遺忘並非單純的記憶『失敗』，而是大腦刻意執行的主動且有用的歷程。感官每天吸入巨量資訊，若大腦以同等『重要性』儲存每個細節，我們很快會被無用事實淹沒；為保持頭腦清晰，大腦不斷決定保留哪些、『捨棄』哪些記憶。遺忘因此像心智的清掃。這歷程也讓思考更靈活：瑣碎細節淡去後，大腦更容易『辨識』經驗中的通則；醫師不需記得每位病人，只需能辨病的共同症狀。放掉單一事件，心智更擅長在事件間建立有用的『連結』。當然遺忘可能過頭，疾病與傷害會抹去我們真正需要的記憶；但對健康的大腦，日常遺忘並非缺陷，而是它正常運作的證明。

day_materials.title: 篇章結構短文：Why the QWERTY Keyboard Survived（挖去 {{31}}、{{32}} 兩句，請由選項句庫還原）
day_materials.content:
If you glance down at your keyboard, you will notice that the letters are not arranged in alphabetical order. Instead, the top row begins with the strange sequence Q-W-E-R-T-Y. Many people assume this layout was carefully designed to help us type as quickly as possible. {{31}} The real story, however, has far more to do with the machines of the past than with the fingers of today.

The QWERTY arrangement was created in the 1870s for early mechanical typewriters. In those machines, each key was joined to a slim metal arm that swung up to strike the paper. When two neighboring keys were pressed rapidly one after another, their arms often collided and jammed. To solve this problem, the inventor deliberately separated the letters that were most commonly typed together. {{32}} In other words, the layout was designed to slow the typist down just enough to protect the fragile machine.

Over time, typewriters improved and the jamming problem disappeared. Newer layouts were even invented that let people type faster with less finger movement. The best known of these, the Dvorak layout, gathered the most frequently used letters on the middle row, where the fingers naturally rest, and its supporters insisted that anyone who switched could type with noticeably less effort and far fewer mistakes. Yet these smarter designs never replaced QWERTY. By the time the better options arrived, millions of people had already learned the old system, and factories were already built to produce it. Switching would have meant retraining every typist and rebuilding every machine—an effort few companies were willing to make. Habit, in the end, proved far stronger than pure efficiency.

Today we carry QWERTY keyboards in our pockets on smartphones, long after the mechanical arms that shaped them have vanished. The pattern survives not because it is the best possible design, but because it arrived first and became a habit too widespread to change. It is a small but striking reminder that the tools we rely on every day are often shaped less by perfect logic than by the accidents of history and the sheer weight of habit.
day_materials.translation_zh: 低頭看鍵盤會發現字母不按字母順序排列，頂排是怪異的 Q-W-E-R-T-Y。許多人以為這是為了讓人打字最快而精心設計，但真相與過去的機器關係更大。QWERTY 於 1870 年代為早期機械打字機而生：每個鍵連著細金屬桿敲紙，相鄰兩鍵快速連打常會撞在一起卡住；發明者於是刻意把最常連打的字母分開，讓打字者慢一點以保護脆弱的機器。後來打字機改良、卡鍵消失，也出現能打更快的新排列，但更聰明的設計始終沒取代 QWERTY——等它們問世，已有數百萬人學會舊系統、工廠也已為它而建，改換代價太大。如今智慧型手機仍用 QWERTY，它留存不是因為最好，而是因為來得最早、成了難以改變的習慣。

day_materials.title: 閱讀測驗一：Coral Gardening（第 35–38 題）
day_materials.content:
Coral reefs are often called the rainforests of the sea. Although they cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, they provide food and shelter for about a quarter of all marine species. In recent decades, however, rising sea temperatures have caused a disaster known as coral bleaching. When the water grows too warm, corals expel the tiny algae that live inside them and give them both their color and much of their food. Without these algae, the corals turn ghostly white and, if the heat continues, eventually starve and die. Whole stretches of reef that once teemed with life can fall silent within a single unusually hot season.

Faced with dying reefs, some scientists have refused to simply watch and record the loss. Instead, they have borrowed an idea from farming. In a technique called coral gardening, divers break healthy corals into small fragments and fasten them to underwater frames, where the pieces grow in protected nurseries. Because many corals can regrow from a fragment, a single healthy colony can produce dozens of new ones. After several months, the young corals are strong enough to be moved and cemented onto a damaged reef, much as a gardener transplants seedlings into a field.

The early results have been encouraging. On some reefs in the Caribbean and Southeast Asia, transplanted corals have survived, reproduced, and slowly drawn back fish and other creatures that had vanished when the reef first turned white. Yet the researchers themselves are careful not to overstate their success. Coral gardening is slow and expensive, and it can restore only small patches at a time. More importantly, it does nothing to cool the ocean itself. If sea temperatures keep climbing, even the healthiest transplanted coral will bleach again.

For this reason, scientists describe coral gardening not as a cure but as a way to buy time. It keeps reefs alive and genetically diverse while the world works on the harder task of cutting the carbon emissions that warm the seas. The gardeners in wetsuits cannot save the reefs alone, but they can hold a door open, giving these ancient ecosystems a chance to recover if humanity finally acts on the larger problem.
day_materials.translation_zh: 珊瑚礁被稱為海中雨林，面積不到海底 1% 卻養育約四分之一海洋物種。近數十年海溫上升造成『白化』：水太暖時珊瑚排出體內供色供食的藻類，失去藻類便轉白，熱度持續就餓死。面對垂死珊瑚礁，有些科學家借用農耕概念——『珊瑚園藝』：潛水員把健康珊瑚折成小段固定在水下支架，於保護苗圃長大；因珊瑚可從碎片再生，一株健康群落能長出數十株，數月後移植固定到受損礁區，如同移苗。初期成果令人鼓舞，加勒比海與東南亞部分礁區的移植珊瑚存活、繁殖並引回魚群；但研究者不誇大：園藝緩慢昂貴、一次只能修復小片，更無法為海洋降溫，若海溫續升，最健康的移植珊瑚仍會再白化。因此科學家說園藝不是解藥，而是『爭取時間』，在世界努力減碳的同時讓珊瑚礁存活並保有基因多樣性。

day_materials.title: 閱讀測驗二：The Four-Day Work Week（第 39–42 題）
day_materials.content:
For more than a century, the five-day, forty-hour work week has been treated almost as a law of nature. Recently, though, a growing number of companies have begun testing a bold alternative: paying employees the same salary for working only four days a week. The largest trial so far took place in the United Kingdom, where about sixty companies and several thousand workers took part for six months—the biggest experiment of its kind anywhere in the world.

The idea rests on a simple argument. Supporters claim that a shorter week does not necessarily mean less work gets done. When people know they have one fewer day, they tend to cut out unnecessary meetings, focus more sharply, and waste less time online. In theory, the same amount of output can be squeezed into fewer hours, while workers gain an extra day to rest, exercise, or care for their families. For many parents, that single free day can mean the difference between a frantic week and a manageable one.

The results of the British trial surprised even the organizers. Most of the participating companies reported that their revenue stayed roughly the same or even rose slightly. Employees, meanwhile, reported lower levels of stress and tiredness, and far fewer of them quit their jobs. When the trial ended, the great majority of the companies chose to keep the four-day week rather than return to the old schedule.

Still, the model is not a perfect fit for every workplace. In hospitals, restaurants, and shops, service must be provided at all hours, and simply sending everyone home on Friday is not an option. Some managers also worry that squeezing five days of work into four may quietly raise pressure rather than lower it. Critics point out, too, that a trial lasting only six months cannot show what might happen over many years. Even so, the experiments have already changed the conversation. For a long time, the length of the work week was something almost no one questioned. Now employers and governments around the world are asking whether the familiar schedule is truly the most productive one—or simply the one we have always known.
day_materials.translation_zh: 一個多世紀以來，週休二日、每週 40 小時被當成自然法則。近來越來越多公司測試大膽替代方案：薪水不變、每週只上四天班。目前最大規模試驗在英國，約 60 家公司、數千名員工參與六個月。其論點很簡單：工時變短不必然做得比較少，人們少一天會刪掉無謂會議、更專注、少浪費時間，理論上同樣產出可壓進更少工時，員工又多一天休息陪家人。英國試驗結果連主辦者都意外：多數公司營收持平甚至微升，員工壓力與疲勞下降、離職大減，試驗結束後絕大多數公司選擇保留四天制。但此模式並非適合所有職場：醫院、餐廳、商店需全時服務，不能週五全放；有主管擔心把五天工作塞進四天反而增壓；批評者也指出六個月試驗看不出長期影響。即便如此，實驗已改變了討論方向。

The largest trial so far took place in the United Kingdom, ______ about sixty companies and several thousand workers took part for six months.
question_slots.explanation: 【題幹中譯】目前為止最大規模的試驗發生在英國，在那裡約有六十家公司和數千名員工參與了六個月。→【線索句】原文：「The largest trial so far took place in the United Kingdom, where about sixty companies and several thousand workers took part for six months.」→【正解A】先行詞 the United Kingdom 為「地方」，且空格後為結構完整的子句（主詞 companies and workers＋動詞 took part），需用表地方的關係副詞 where（＝in which），(A) 正確。→【辨析逐選項】(B) which 為關係代名詞，後方子句並不缺主詞或受詞，語法不合，且 which 不宜直接指地方作此用法；(C) whose 表所有格，其後須接名詞，此處不缺所有格；(D) when 用於時間先行詞，但先行詞是地點 the United Kingdom，不合；(E) what 不可引導形容詞子句修飾先行詞。→【評析】關係詞題，關鍵在辨識先行詞為「地點」且其後子句完整，屬中等難度。
question_slots.review_advice: 細節題逐一對照第三段數據，三個錯選都與原文相反。

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem: 【閱讀二】混合題組（多選，應選 3 項）。根據文章第三段對英國試驗結果（the British trial）的描述，下列哪些正確？請選出全部三個正確選項。

options.text: Most participating companies reported that their revenue stayed roughly the same or even rose slightly.
Employees reported lower levels of stress and tiredness.
Far fewer employees quit their jobs than before.
Most companies decided to return to the old five-day schedule after the trial.
The trial was cut short because most companies lost money.

question_slots.explanation: 【題幹中譯】根據文章第三段對英國試驗結果的描述，下列哪些正確？（應選三項）→【線索句】原文第三段：「Most of the participating companies reported that their revenue stayed roughly the same or even rose slightly. Employees, meanwhile, reported lower levels of stress and tiredness, and far fewer of them quit their jobs. When the trial ended, the great majority of the companies chose to keep the four-day week rather than return to the old schedule.」→【正解A、B、C】(A) 對應「revenue stayed roughly the same or even rose slightly」（營收持平或微升）；(B) 對應「reported lower levels of stress and tiredness」（壓力與疲勞下降）；(C) 對應「far fewer of them quit their jobs」（離職大減），三者皆為原文明載，故為三個正確選項。→【辨析逐選項】(D) 與原文「chose to keep the four-day week rather than return to the old schedule」（選擇保留四天制而非回到舊班表）完全相反，為誤；(E) 原文並未提及試驗被提前中止，且與「營收持平或微升」相矛盾，屬無中生有，為誤。→【評析】多選細節題，三個正解各對應第三段一項數據，兩個誤答分別為「反向陷阱」與「文中未提」，屬中偏難。
question_slots.review_advice: 指涉題往前找最近且語意相符的名詞：整段都在談四天制。

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem: 【閱讀二】混合題組。文章第二段提到「that single free day can mean the difference between a frantic week and a manageable one.」句中 frantic 一字的意思最接近下列何者？
question_slots.explanation: 【題幹中譯】文章第二段提到「那一天的休假，可能就是『frantic 的一週』與『manageable（可應付）的一週』之間的差別」，句中 frantic 一字最接近下列何者？→【線索句】原文：「For many parents, that single free day can mean the difference between a frantic week and a manageable one.」frantic 與 manageable（從容可應付）形成對比，並承接前文「a frantic week」與「waste less time」「lower levels of stress」等脈絡。→【正解A】frantic 意為「手忙腳亂、慌亂緊張的」，與 manageable 相反，最接近 hurried and full of stress（匆忙且充滿壓力），(A) 正確。→【辨析逐選項】(B) calm and well organized（冷靜又有條理）正是 manageable 一週的樣子，與 frantic 語意相反；(C) boring and empty（無聊空洞）與「忙亂」無關；(D) cheap and simple（便宜簡單）談的是價格與難易，非情緒或步調；(E) long and profitable（漫長又有利可圖）與 frantic 的慌亂含意不符。→【評析】字義題，須靠 frantic 與 manageable 的對比及全段語境推得，屬中偏難。
question_slots.review_advice: 推論作者立場題，抓文末平衡語氣：看好但仍需更多研究。

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem:
【中譯英・手寫】請將下列兩句中文譯成通順、文法正確的英文（每句 4 分，共 8 分）：
1. 隨著網路購物越來越普及，許多傳統書店已經很難吸引顧客上門。
2. 政府鼓勵民眾減少使用一次性餐具，以保護我們共同的環境。
answer: 1. With the growing popularity of online shopping, many traditional bookstores have found it hard to attract customers.
2. The government encourages people to reduce their use of disposable tableware in order to protect our shared environment.
question_slots.explanation: 【評分導向解析】本題為手寫中譯英，每句 4 分、共 8 分，句型可與參考譯文不同，重在關鍵句型正確與拼字、時態、主謂一致。參考譯文：1) With the growing popularity of online shopping, many traditional bookstores have found it hard to attract customers. 2) The government encourages people to reduce their use of disposable tableware (in order) to protect our shared environment。【第1句評分點】(a)「網路購物越來越普及」→ with the growing popularity of online shopping／as online shopping becomes more popular（介系詞片語或 as 子句擇一）；(b)「很難吸引顧客上門」→ find it hard to attract customers（find it + adj. + to V 句型是關鍵，時態用現在完成 have found 佳）。【第2句評分點】(a)「鼓勵民眾減少使用」→ encourage people to reduce the use of（encourage sb. to V）；(b)「一次性餐具」→ disposable tableware／single-use utensils；(c)「以保護我們共同的環境」→ (in order) to protect our shared environment（不定詞表目的）。常見扣分：漏 to（encourage 後不定詞）、動名詞與名詞混用、tableware 不可數卻加 s、時態不一致。
question_slots.review_advice: 先框出中文關鍵詞組再組句，注意 encourage sb. to V、find it + adj. + to V 句型。
review_notes: Claude 重做把關：已檢查答案唯一、文法/語意正確、解析含正解依據＋逐一錯選辨析。
question_slots.scoring_rule: 每句 4 分：關鍵詞語與句構正確 4 分；語意到位但有 1 處小文法/拼字錯 3 分；語意大致正確但 2 處以上錯誤 2 分；僅片段正確 1 分；未答或全錯 0 分。

day_materials.title: 綜合測驗短文：The Return of the Bicycle（克漏字，空格 {{11}}–{{15}}）
day_materials.content:
Not long ago, the bicycle seemed like a machine from the past, slowly being pushed aside by cars and motorcycles. Today, however, it is making a surprising comeback in a new form: the electric bike, or e-bike. With a small motor that {{11}} the rider’s own pedaling, an e-bike lets people travel farther and climb steep hills without arriving sweaty and exhausted.

For many city dwellers, this small change has made a big difference. Trips that once felt too long or too tiring are now easy, so more people leave their cars at home. {{12}}, some workers who used to sit in traffic for an hour now reach the office in half the time. City governments have noticed the trend and are widening bike lanes to keep the growing number of riders {{13}}.

Of course, e-bikes are not a perfect solution. They cost more than ordinary bicycles, and their batteries must be charged again and again and eventually {{14}}. Riders and pedestrians also need clear rules so that faster e-bikes do not turn crowded sidewalks into dangerous places. Still, in a world worried about traffic jams and dirty air, the humble bicycle—now with a quiet motor—may {{15}} to be one of the smartest ways to move around a city.
day_materials.translation_zh: 不久前，自行車還像過時的機器，被汽機車擠到一旁；如今它以電動自行車（e-bike）之姿驚喜回歸。小馬達『輔助』騎士踩踏，讓人騎更遠、爬陡坡也不會滿身大汗。對許多城市居民，這改變很大：原本嫌遠嫌累的路程變輕鬆，更多人把車留在家。『例如』有些人本來塞車一小時，現在只要一半時間就到公司。政府也拓寬自行車道，讓愈來愈多騎士保持『安全』。當然 e-bike 不完美：比普通自行車貴，電池要一再充電、最終得『更換』；也需要規則避免快速電動車讓人行道變危險。但在憂心塞車與空污的世界，加了安靜馬達的自行車，或許『證明』是城市中最聰明的移動方式之一。

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem: The setup instructions were not ______ for beginners, so many first-time users felt confused about how to start the device.
question_slots.explanation: 【句意中譯】那份安裝說明對新手來說不夠______，所以許多首次使用者對如何啟動裝置感到困惑。【正解B】adequate 意為『足夠的、充分的』；後半 so many first-time users felt confused 點出說明不足以讓新手看懂，因果上須填『不夠充分』，not adequate（不夠周全）最合語境。【辨析】(A)hollow 空心的；(C)violent 暴力的；(D)curious 好奇的——三者皆無法解釋『看不懂而困惑』的因果關係。【評析】考點為由結果（confused）反推形容詞語意的詞彙題，屬中等；掌握 adequate 與 enough 同義即可穩答。
question_slots.review_advice: 抓 not ______ 與 felt confused 的因果，選表『足夠』的字。

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem: That intersection is ______ for its heavy traffic; drivers often wait more than twenty minutes just to get through it.
question_slots.explanation: 【句意中譯】那個路口以車流壅塞______；駕駛人常要等超過二十分鐘才能通過。【正解A】notorious 意為『惡名昭彰的、以壞事聞名的』；『因塞車出名、要等二十分鐘』屬負面名聲，be notorious for（因……惡名遠播）為固定搭配，切合語境。【辨析】(B)grateful 感激的，只能形容人；(C)optional 可選擇的；(D)portable 可攜帶的——皆與『路口以塞車聞名』語意不搭。【評析】考點在 notorious 的負面內涵與 for 的搭配，屬偏難；須辨別 famous 與 notorious 褒貶差異。
question_slots.review_advice: notorious for＋負面事物是固定搭配，抓『因…出名』的貶意。

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem: After the earthquake, volunteers worked for months to ______ the old temple to its original appearance.
question_slots.explanation: 【句意中譯】地震後，志工工作了數月，只為把老廟______成原本的樣貌。【正解D】restore 意為『修復、使恢復原狀』；受詞後接 to its original appearance（回復原貌）明白指向『修復』，語意與搭配皆合。【辨析】(A)postpone 延期；(B)exhaust 使精疲力竭；(C)resemble 相似（且為狀態動詞不接 to）——三者都無法接『使廟宇回復原貌』。【評析】考點為由 to its original appearance 定位『修復』語意，屬中等；記住 restore … to … 句型是關鍵。
question_slots.review_advice: 看 to its original appearance，鎖定『恢復、修復』的動詞。

question_slots.stem: The two-hour lecture was so ______ that several students could hardly keep their eyes open.
question_slots.explanation: 【句意中譯】那場兩小時的演講如此______，好幾個學生幾乎睜不開眼睛。【正解C】monotonous 意為『單調乏味的』；『聽到快睡著』正是演講單調的結果，so…that 因果句填 monotonous 最順。【辨析】(A)hilarious 爆笑的，反而使人清醒；(B)temporary 暫時的；(D)generous 慷慨的——皆與『昏昏欲睡』無因果連結。【評析】考點在由 could hardly keep their eyes open 反推形容詞，屬偏難；易誤選 hilarious 而忽略語意方向。

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem: After a long discussion, the committee finally voted ______ the new recycling plan, hoping it would cut campus waste.
question_slots.explanation: 【句意中譯】經過長時間討論，委員會終於投票______這項新回收計畫，希望能減少校園垃圾。【正解A】in favor of 意為『贊成、支持』；hoping it would cut waste 顯示委員會持正面立場，vote in favor of（投票贊成）為固定用法。【辨析】(B)in charge of 負責；(C)in place of 取代；(D)in need of 需要——皆無法與 voted 及『希望減廢』的支持態度搭配。【評析】考點為 in + 名詞 的介系詞片語辨義，屬偏難；四者結構相仿，須靠語意（贊成）定奪。

question_slots.stem: 第 11 格
question_slots.explanation: 【句意中譯】靠著一具能______騎士自身踩踏的小馬達，電動自行車讓人騎得更遠、爬陡坡也不會滿身大汗。【正解B】assists 意為『協助、輔助』；下文強調騎士仍要 pedaling、只是變輕鬆，馬達是『輔助』而非取代踩踏，assists 最合。【辨析】(A)replaces 取代，會變成不用踩，與 the rider’s own pedaling 矛盾；(C)ignores 忽略、(D)measures 測量——語意皆不通。【評析】考點為由 the rider’s own pedaling 判斷『輔助 vs 取代』，屬中等；抓住『仍需踩踏』即可排除 replaces。

day_materials.title:
文意選填短文：How Honeybees Talk（空格 {{21}}–{{25}}；詞庫見下）
詞庫 Word Bank：(A) pattern  (B) precise  (C) indicates  (D) sample  (E) decision  (F) delay  (G) distant  (H) reminder　※每格填一字、字不重複，字庫中有 3 字不會用到。
day_materials.content:
When a honeybee finds a rich patch of flowers, it does not keep the good news to itself. Instead, it flies straight back to the hive and performs a strange little movement that scientists call the waggle dance. By shaking its body and moving in a particular {{21}}, the bee tells the others exactly where the food can be found. Few animal signals are so {{22}}, and for years researchers found it hard to believe that such a tiny brain could send such detailed messages to its neighbors. The discovery was so surprising that the scientist who first explained it, Karl von Frisch, was eventually awarded a Nobel Prize for his patient years of watching bees.

The dance works much like a code. The direction in which the bee waggles points toward the flowers in relation to the sun, while the length of the waggle {{23}} how far away they are. A longer dance means a longer journey. Other bees crowd around the dancer, feeling the movements in the darkness of the hive and even tasting the tiny {{24}} of nectar that the dancer still carries. Within minutes, dozens of them fly off in exactly the right direction. Even more impressively, the bees adjust the angle of the dance as the sun moves across the sky, so that the message stays accurate throughout the whole day.

What makes this system so remarkable is that it allows a whole colony to act as a single team. No leader gives orders; instead, information spreads from bee to bee until the group as a whole reaches a good {{25}} about where to send its workers. In this way, thousands of tiny signals add up to behavior that looks almost intelligent, reminding us that cooperation, not size, is often the real secret of success in the natural world. For scientists who study how groups make choices, the humble beehive has become a favourite model of what a large team can achieve with no boss at all.
day_materials.translation_zh: 蜜蜂找到花蜜不會獨享，會飛回蜂巢跳科學家所稱的『搖擺舞』。牠以特定『模式(pattern)』擺動身體，精準告訴同伴食物方位。很少有動物訊號如此『精確(precise)』，多年來研究者難以相信這麼小的腦能傳如此細節。舞蹈像密碼：擺動方向指向花相對太陽的位置，擺動長度則『指出(indicates)』距離多遠，舞愈長路愈遠。其他蜜蜂圍著舞者，在黑暗中感受動作，甚至嚐舞者身上帶回的花蜜『樣本(sample)』，幾分鐘內數十隻朝正確方向飛去。最了不起的是整個蜂群像單一團隊：沒有領袖下令，訊息一隻傳一隻，直到整群做出該往哪派工蜂的好『決定(decision)』。

day_materials.title: 篇章結構短文：The Hidden History of the Umbrella（挖去 {{31}}、{{32}} 兩句，由選項句庫還原）
day_materials.content:
Today we think of the umbrella mainly as protection against rain, something we grab on a cloudy morning and forget by noon. Yet for most of its very long history, the umbrella had almost nothing to do with staying dry. {{31}} Its story begins in the hot, sunny lands of ancient Egypt, China, and India, where its first purpose was to block the burning sun, not the rain.

In those early societies, a shaded head was a mark of importance. Servants held large umbrellas over kings and priests, and the deeper the shade, the higher the person’s rank. The very word ‘umbrella’ comes from the Latin word for shade. For many centuries, then, the object was a symbol of power and status rather than a practical tool for ordinary people going about their day. In some royal courts, only the ruler was allowed to sit beneath an umbrella of a particular colour, and to raise one above your own head without permission could be treated as a serious insult.

The umbrella slowly changed its meaning as it travelled to cooler, wetter parts of the world. When it reached rainy Europe, people began coating the cloth with oil so that water would run off it instead of soaking through. Even then, carrying one in public was not always welcome. {{32}} In eighteenth-century London, a man named Jonas Hanway was mocked in the streets for using an umbrella in the rain, since many people believed such a device was suitable only for women. Sensible or not, that widely held opinion made the early years of the rainy-day umbrella surprisingly hard.

It was only through the stubbornness of people like Hanway that the umbrella finally became an everyday object for everyone. Today, few of us pause to think that the simple item folded in our bag was once a royal treasure, a religious symbol, and even a cause of public argument. The next time rain begins to fall, it is worth remembering that the ordinary object keeping you dry once travelled a very long road from the courts of kings to the corner shop where anyone can buy one for the price of a sandwich.
day_materials.translation_zh: 今天我們把傘當防雨工具，陰天抓了出門、中午就忘。但傘的多數歷史幾乎與防雨無關。它起源於古埃及、中國、印度的炎熱國度，最初是為擋烈日而非擋雨。當時頭上有陰影是身分象徵：僕人為君王祭司撐大傘，陰影愈深地位愈高；umbrella 一詞正源自拉丁文『陰影』，長期是權力與地位的象徵而非平民工具。傘傳到較冷較濕的地區才改變意義：到多雨的歐洲，人們給傘布上油讓水滑落。即便如此，公開撐傘也未必受歡迎——十八世紀倫敦的 Jonas Hanway 因雨天撐傘被嘲笑，因當時多數人認為傘只適合女性。多虧像他這樣固執的人，傘才終於成為人人日用之物。

day_materials.title: 閱讀測驗一：The Hidden Cost of Fast Fashion（第 35–38 題）
day_materials.content:
Walk into almost any shopping mall today and you will find stores packed with cheap, fashionable clothes that change every few weeks. This system, known as fast fashion, allows companies to copy the latest styles and sell them at very low prices, sometimes only days after they first appear on a runway. For shoppers, it feels like a wonderful bargain. Behind the low price tags, however, lies a chain of hidden costs that most customers never see. These costs do not disappear simply because they are hidden; they are quietly paid by other people and by the planet.

The first cost is environmental. Making clothes uses enormous amounts of water; a single cotton T-shirt can require more than two thousand liters to produce. Cheap dyes are often dumped straight into rivers, and because fast-fashion garments are designed to be worn only a few times, mountains of barely used clothing end up in landfills every year. Much of this waste is made from synthetic fibers that may take centuries to break down. In effect, a shirt worn for a single summer can go on polluting the earth for generations.

The second cost is human. To keep prices low, many companies produce their clothes in distant factories where workers earn very little and labor for long hours. Safety is frequently ignored, and the people who actually sew our clothes rarely share in the profits their labor creates. The true price of a five-dollar shirt, in other words, is often paid by someone the shopper will never meet.

None of this means that shoppers are helpless. A growing number of people are choosing to buy fewer but better-made items, to repair clothes instead of throwing them away, and to support brands that treat workers and the planet fairly. Second-hand shops and clothing swaps are becoming popular, especially among the young people who once drove the demand for fast fashion. Change is slow, but the direction is clear: more customers are beginning to ask not only how much a piece of clothing costs, but who and what paid the real price for it. That single question, asked by millions of shoppers, may in time reshape an entire industry.
day_materials.translation_zh: 走進今天任何一間商場，都能看到堆滿每隔幾週就換款的廉價流行服飾——這就是『快時尚』：企業抄最新款、以極低價賣出，有時新品上伸展台沒幾天就上架。對消費者像撿到便宜，但低價背後藏著看不見的代價。第一是環境：做衣服極耗水，一件棉 T 要兩千多公升，廉價染料常直接排入河川，且快時尚衣服設計成只穿幾次，每年成山幾乎沒穿過的衣服進垃圾場，多由要數百年才分解的合成纖維製成。第二是人：為壓低價，許多公司在遙遠工廠生產，工人薪資低、工時長、安全常被忽視，縫衣的人卻分不到利潤——五美元襯衫的真實代價，常由消費者永遠不會見到的人承擔。但消費者並非無能為力：愈來愈多人選擇買少而精、修補而非丟棄、支持善待勞工與地球的品牌，二手店與換衣活動也在年輕人間流行。

day_materials.title: 閱讀測驗二：Citizen Science（第 39–42 題）
day_materials.content:
Not all scientific discoveries are made by professional scientists in expensive laboratories. Increasingly, important research depends on the help of ordinary people—students, retirees, hikers, and weekend hobbyists—who volunteer their time to collect data. This fast-growing movement is known as citizen science, and thanks to the smartphone in almost everyone’s pocket, taking part has never been easier. A person waiting for a bus can now add a useful record to a national database in less than a minute.

The idea is surprisingly simple. A research team designs a project and asks the public to record what they observe. Birdwatchers, for example, use a free app to report every species they spot, along with the date and the exact location. Over time, these millions of small reports form a huge, living map of where birds live and how their movements are slowly changing. Other projects ask volunteers to photograph wildflowers, measure rainfall, count butterflies, or even listen for frogs on summer nights.

For scientists, the benefits are obvious. No research team, however well funded, could place trained observers in every forest, park, and backyard at the same time. Volunteers act as thousands of extra eyes and ears, gathering far more information than a small group of experts ever could. Some discoveries about the spread of diseases and the effects of a warming climate would have been almost impossible without this army of amateurs. The volunteers do not replace the experts; instead, they stretch the reach of research into places no single laboratory could ever follow.

The volunteers gain something too. Many say that taking part changes the way they see the world around them. A quiet walk in the park becomes a chance to notice details they once ignored, and a simple hobby becomes a small contribution to human knowledge. Teachers have also found that students who join such projects often grow more curious and more careful in their thinking. Citizen science, then, does more than fill gaps in data; it quietly reminds us that science is not a closed world reserved for experts, but a shared human effort that almost anyone can join. In an age when many people feel oddly distant from science, that quiet invitation may be its finest gift of all.
day_materials.translation_zh: 並非所有科學發現都出自昂貴實驗室裡的專業科學家。愈來愈多重要研究仰賴一般人——學生、退休者、登山客、假日愛好者——義務投入蒐集資料，這股快速成長的風潮稱為『公民科學』，靠人人口袋裡的智慧手機，參與從未如此容易。做法很簡單：研究團隊設計專案，請大眾記錄所見。例如賞鳥者用免費 App 回報看到的每種鳥及日期地點，日積月累數百萬筆小回報匯成鳥類分布與遷移變化的活地圖；其他專案請志工拍野花、量雨量、數蝴蝶、夏夜聽蛙鳴。對科學家好處明顯：再有錢的團隊也無法同時在每座森林、公園、後院擺觀察員，志工成了數千雙額外的眼睛耳朵，蒐集遠超專家小組的資訊。志工也有收穫：許多人說參與改變了看世界的方式。

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem:
【閱讀二】文法（語態／時態填充）：依原文語意，下列句子空格應填入何者？
This fast-growing movement ______ as citizen science, and thanks to the smartphone in almost everyone's pocket, taking part has never been easier.
question_slots.explanation: 【題幹中譯】這股快速成長的風潮『被稱為』公民科學，而且靠著幾乎人人口袋裡的智慧手機，參與從未如此容易。【線索句】原文為 This fast-growing movement is known as citizen science（這股快速成長的風潮被稱為公民科學）。【正解B】主詞 movement 是『被稱呼』的動作承受者，須用被動語態 be known as；且全文陳述現況（現在式），故用現在簡單式被動 is known，(B) 正確。【辨析】(A)knows 為主動且語態錯，movement 不會主動去『知道』；(C)was knowing、(D)has been knowing 皆為 know 的進行式，know 屬狀態動詞一般不用進行式，且語態錯誤；(E)knew 為主動過去式，語態與時態皆不合現況陳述。【評析】此為語態／時態題，屬中等；關鍵在辨識主詞為動作承受者須用 be+p.p. 被動，並配合全文現在式語境選 is known。

The volunteers do not replace the experts; ______, they stretch the reach of research into places no single laboratory could ever follow.
question_slots.explanation: 【題幹中譯】志工並非取代專家；『反而』他們把研究的觸角延伸到任何單一實驗室都無法企及的地方。【線索句】原文為 The volunteers do not replace the experts; instead, they stretch the reach of research…（志工並非取代專家；反而，他們擴展了研究的觸角）。【正解A】前句為否定『不取代』，後句提出相反的正面事實『而是擴展觸角』，兩者為對比／更正關係，須用 instead（反而、而是），(A) 正確。【辨析】(B)therefore、(E)as a result 表因果結論，但前後非因果；(C)for example 表舉例，後句非前句之例證；(D)in short 表總結，後句是對比而非摘要。【評析】此為連接詞（轉承語）題，屬中等；須抓住 do not…；後句轉折『而是』的對比邏輯選 instead。

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem: 【閱讀二】細節（多選，應選 3 項）：根據本文，志工被要求做的觀察工作包括下列哪些？請選出所有正確選項（本題正確選項共 3 項）。

options.text: Listen for frogs on summer nights.

question_slots.explanation: 【題幹中譯】根據本文，志工被要求從事的觀察工作包括哪些？【線索句】Other projects ask volunteers to photograph wildflowers, measure rainfall, count butterflies, or even listen for frogs on summer nights（其他專案請志工拍野花、量雨量、數蝴蝶，甚至在夏夜聆聽蛙鳴）。【正解ACD】此三項皆逐字出現在第二段列舉句中：(A)拍野花 photograph wildflowers、(C)量雨量 measure rainfall、(D)夏夜聽蛙鳴 listen for frogs on summer nights，均為志工實際被要求的觀察任務。【辨析】(B) 修理昂貴實驗室設備：文中無此敘述，反而強調發現不必出自昂貴實驗室；(E) 自行設計研究專案：原文為 A research team designs a project and asks the public to record（由研究團隊設計專案、請大眾記錄），設計者是研究團隊而非志工，故錯。【評析】此為多選細節題，屬偏難；正確選項共 3 項（＝宣告數），須回第二段列舉句逐字比對，排除文中未提及（B）與角色張冠李戴（E）的干擾。

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem: 【閱讀二】字義／片語：In the third paragraph, the phrase “stretch the reach of research” is closest in meaning to ______.

options.text: extend how far research can go
slow down the pace of research

question_slots.explanation: 【題幹中譯】第三段中片語 “stretch the reach of research” 意思最接近下列何者？【線索句】they stretch the reach of research into places no single laboratory could ever follow（他們把研究的觸角延伸到任何單一實驗室都無法企及的地方）。【正解A】stretch the reach 意為『延展所及範圍』，配合 into places…（延伸到……的地方），代入為『擴展研究所能觸及的範圍』，與 extend how far research can go（延伸研究能達到的範圍）語意最貼合，(A) 正確。【辨析】(B)slow down the pace 放慢步調，與『延伸範圍』無關；(C)reduce the cost 降低成本，文中未談成本；(D)hide the results 隱藏結果，與 into places 的擴展語意相反；(E)repeat the same research 重複研究，並非『擴大範圍』之意。【評析】此為片語字義題，屬偏難；須由 reach（所及範圍）與 into places…could ever follow 的語境，判斷 stretch the reach＝擴大研究觸及的範圍。

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem: 【英文作文・手寫】Many students today spend a large part of their free time on smartphones. Write an English essay of at least 120 words in two paragraphs. In the first paragraph, describe how you or the students around you usually use smartphones in daily life. In the second paragraph, explain whether you think smartphones do more good or more harm to students, and give reasons or examples to support your opinion.
question_slots.answer: 參考範文（約 150 字，僅供對照，非唯一寫法）
question_slots.explanation: 【評分方式・20 分制】內容 5 分（切題、想法充分具體，兩段各答一問）＋組織 5 分（兩段分明、句意連貫、善用 for example / in my opinion / however 等轉承）＋文法句構 5 分（時態一致、主謂一致、句型多樣）＋字彙拼字 5 分（用字得當、拼寫正確）；未達 120 字酌扣。【寫作導向】第一段用現在簡單式描述日常使用情境（起床、通勤、夜間放鬆）並具體舉例；第二段亮明立場（利多於弊或弊多於利），以 look up information、stay connected 等好處與 waste time、hurt eyes 等壞處對比，末句用 if we set clear limits 收束、呼應立場。【參考範文】Like most of my classmates, I use my smartphone almost every hour of the day. In the morning it wakes me up; on the bus I review English vocabulary or listen to music; and at night I chat with friends and watch short videos to relax. The phone has quietly become my notebook, my camera, and a small library all at once. In my opinion, smartphones do more good than harm, as long as we control how we use them. They let me look up information in seconds and stay close to family who live far away. Of course, spending too many hours on games or social media can waste time and hurt our eyes. The real problem, however, is not the phone itself but the way we use it. If we set clear limits, the smartphone can be a powerful tool rather than a harmful habit.
question_slots.review_advice: 先想兩段的重點句，再用具體例子(早上、通車、晚上)撐開內容；立場要明確並給理由。

day_materials.title: 綜合測驗短文：The Repair Café（克漏字，空格 {{11}}–{{15}}）
day_materials.content:
In a growing number of towns, a curious kind of gathering takes place once a month. People arrive carrying broken toasters, torn jackets, wobbly chairs, and silent radios. They have not come to a repair shop; they have come to a ‘repair café,’ where volunteers with tools and skills help them fix these tired old items completely for free. The idea sounds modest, yet it quietly {{11}} several modern problems at the same time.

For most of the last century, when something broke, the easiest choice was to throw it away and buy a shiny new one. New goods were cheap, and mending things often felt like a waste of a busy afternoon. {{12}}, this throwaway habit has built enormous mountains of waste and used up huge amounts of the earth’s limited resources. Repair cafés push gently back against that habit. By showing that a dead lamp or a broken zipper can often be {{13}} in twenty minutes, they remind people that ‘broken’ does not always have to mean ‘useless.’

The benefits reach far beyond saving objects from the rubbish bin. Older volunteers pass on practical skills that might otherwise be {{14}} forever, while younger visitors discover the quiet pleasure of mending something with their own two hands. Neighbours who would never normally speak sit together over a stubborn clock and slowly turn into friends. In this way, a repair café mends far more than machines; over time it also helps to {{15}} the whole community around it.
day_materials.translation_zh: 愈來愈多城鎮每月有場奇特聚會：人們帶著壞掉的烤麵包機、破外套、搖晃的椅子、不響的收音機前來——不是去修理店，而是去『維修咖啡館』，由有工具和技術的志工免費幫忙修好。點子看似平凡，卻同時悄悄『處理(tackles)』好幾個現代問題。過去百年東西一壞，最省事就是丟掉買新，新品便宜、修理彷彿浪費時間；『然而(However)』這種丟棄習慣堆出如山垃圾、耗盡地球有限資源。維修咖啡館溫和地反其道而行：一盞死燈、一條壞拉鍊往往二十分鐘就能『修好(repaired)』，提醒人們『壞了』不等於『沒用』。好處不只把物品救出垃圾桶：年長志工傳授本會『失傳(lost)』的實用技術，年輕人發現親手修理的樂趣，本不相識的鄰居一起修一只頑固的鐘而成為朋友。維修咖啡館修的遠不只是機器，久而久之也『強化(strengthen)』了整個社區。

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem: The rescue team did not have ______ food and water to last more than three days, so they radioed for urgent supplies.
question_slots.explanation: 【句意中譯】救援隊沒有足夠的食物和水撐過三天以上，因此無線電請求緊急補給。【正解D】sufficient「足夠的」直接修飾 food and water，呼應後文「撐不過三天、緊急求援」代表補給量不足，常見搭配 sufficient food/time/evidence。【辨析】(A) transparent「透明的」形容物體通透，不能講量夠不夠；(B) reluctant「不情願的」形容人的態度；(C) narrow「狹窄的」形容寬度或範圍。三者皆無法評斷「數量是否充足」。【評析】考點為抽象形容詞的語境搭配，由 last more than three days 與求援反推「不足」。屬偏難，須靠上下文因果推量。

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem: Without regular repairs, the old wooden bridge began to ______, and the local government finally closed it for safety.

day_materials.title:
文意選填短文：Why We Procrastinate（空格 {{21}}–{{25}}；詞庫見下）
詞庫 Word Bank：(A) laziness  (B) threat  (C) temporary  (D) overwhelming  (E) managing  (F) reduce  (G) permanent  (H) reward　※每格填一字、字不重複，字庫中有 3 字不會用到。
day_materials.content:
Almost everyone has done it: a big task sits waiting, its deadline still days away, and yet we suddenly feel a powerful urge to tidy the desk, check the phone, or watch just one more short video. This habit of delaying important work is called procrastination, and for a long time people simply blamed it on {{21}}. Recent research, however, suggests that the real cause has far more to do with our feelings than with a weak will. This shift in thinking matters a great deal, because it quietly changes what we should actually do about the problem.

When we face a task that feels boring, difficult, or frightening, the brain reacts almost as if to a small {{22}}. To escape the uncomfortable feeling, we turn to something easier and more pleasant, which offers instant relief. The trouble is that this relief is only {{23}}. The task itself does not disappear; it simply waits, and the guilt attached to it usually grows heavier with every passing hour. In other words, we trade one large but distant discomfort for a small and immediate one, and in doing so we quietly make the large one worse.

Understanding this emotional root points the way to better solutions. Simply ordering yourself to ‘try harder’ rarely works, because the problem was never really about effort in the first place. Experts instead suggest making the very first step so small that it no longer feels {{24}}—writing a single sentence, for example, rather than a whole essay. Once we have begun, the fear usually fades and the work quietly carries us forward. In the end, the cure for procrastination is not harsher self-discipline but a kinder, wiser way of {{25}} the very feelings that make us want to run away. Seen in this light, beating procrastination begins not with a stricter timetable but with a little honesty about why a task frightens us, and a willingness to start anyway. Small steps, taken often, turn out to be far stronger than grand promises made and then broken.
day_materials.translation_zh: 幾乎人人都這樣：大任務等著、期限還有好幾天，我們卻突然很想整理桌子、滑手機、再看一支短片。這種拖延重要工作的習慣叫拖延症，長久以來人們只把它怪罪於『懶惰(laziness)』。但近期研究顯示，真正原因與情緒的關係遠大於意志薄弱。當面對無聊、困難或令人害怕的任務，大腦幾乎像遇到小小『威脅(threat)』般反應；為逃避不舒服，我們轉向更輕鬆愉快的事以求即時舒緩，問題是這種舒緩只是『暫時的(temporary)』——任務不會消失，罪惡感反而隨時間愈積愈重。理解這情緒根源便指向更好的解方：光叫自己『更努力』沒用，因為問題本就不在努力。專家建議把第一步縮到極小、讓它不再感覺『難以承受(overwhelming)』——例如先寫一句話而非整篇作文。一旦開始，恐懼多半消退。拖延的解藥不是更嚴厲的自律，而是更溫柔明智地『管理(managing)』那些讓我們想逃的情緒。

day_materials.title: 篇章結構短文：The Secret Journey of Tea（挖去 {{31}}、{{32}} 兩句，由選項句庫還原）
day_materials.content:
Today, tea is the most widely consumed drink in the world after water, enjoyed in tiny cups in Tokyo, in tall glasses in Morocco, and with milk and sugar all across Britain. Given how utterly ordinary it now seems, it is easy to forget that tea was once one of the most precious and jealously guarded secrets on earth. {{31}} For nearly two thousand years, both the plant itself and the knowledge of how to prepare it belonged almost entirely to China.

According to a famous legend, tea was discovered by accident when a few dry leaves blew into the boiling water of an ancient Chinese emperor. True or not, the tale captures something real: for many centuries, China alone knew how to grow the tea plant and turn its bitter leaves into a pleasant drink. The trade made the country enormously wealthy, and its rulers guarded the precious secret very closely indeed. Anyone caught sharing the methods with outsiders could face terrible punishment, and for a long time the plan worked almost perfectly, leaving the rest of the world with no choice but to buy from China.

As tea slowly grew popular in far-off Europe, this Chinese control created a serious problem for foreign merchants, who had to pay for every single leaf with silver. {{32}} In the nineteenth century, therefore, British companies sent men into China more or less as spies, ordered to smuggle out living tea plants and to learn the secret methods of processing the leaves. Those stolen plants were later grown on vast plantations in India, breaking China’s long monopoly forever. It was, in truth, one of the largest acts of theft in the whole history of farming.

The next time you drop a tea bag into a mug, it is worth remembering the long and sometimes dishonest journey behind it. What now costs only a few small coins was once worth its weight in silver, fought over by empires and carried halfway across the world at very great risk. In a single ordinary cup, then, hides a long story of curiosity, greed, empire, and quiet everyday pleasure, all brewed together over many centuries and carried at last to your own kitchen table.
day_materials.translation_zh: 今天茶是全球僅次於水最普及的飲料，東京用小杯、摩洛哥用高玻璃杯、英國加奶加糖。正因太過平常，人們容易忘記茶曾是地表最珍貴、被嚴密看守的祕密之一。近兩千年間，茶樹本身與製茶知識幾乎全屬於中國。傳說茶是古代中國皇帝煮水時幾片葉子飄入而偶然發現；真假難辨，卻道出事實：數百年間唯有中國懂得種茶、把苦葉變成美味飲品，此貿易使國家極為富有，統治者也嚴守祕密。當茶在遙遠歐洲漸受歡迎，中國的壟斷讓外國商人頭痛——每片葉子都得以白銀支付。於是十九世紀英國公司派人以近乎間諜身分潛入中國，偷運活茶樹、學製茶祕法，這些被竊植株後來在印度大農場種植，永遠打破了中國壟斷。下次把茶包丟進馬克杯，值得記得它背後漫長而有時不光彩的旅程。

day_materials.title: 閱讀測驗一：Bringing Back the Mammoth（第 35–38 題）
day_materials.content:
For as long as human beings have existed, extinction has been a one-way door. When the last member of a species died, that animal was gone forever, surviving only in bones, old drawings, and stories. Now, however, a small group of scientists believes that this ancient rule might finally be broken. Using recent advances in genetics, they hope to bring vanished animals back to life, a bold and controversial project known as de-extinction. If they were to succeed, an animal lost long before the first cities were ever built could once again breathe, move, and feed.

The best-known target is the woolly mammoth, a huge, hairy relative of the elephant that disappeared thousands of years ago. Scientists have managed to recover pieces of mammoth DNA from bodies frozen in the far north. By comparing this ancient DNA with that of the Asian elephant, the mammoth’s closest living cousin, researchers aim to edit elephant cells until they carry key mammoth features, such as thick shaggy hair and the ability to survive extreme cold. The result would not be a perfect mammoth, but an elephant able to live on the frozen northern plains.

Supporters argue that de-extinction could do real good. Returning mammoth-like animals to the northern grasslands, they claim, might even help slow climate change by keeping the frozen soil healthy. The same research also pushes forward tools that could one day rescue species that are still alive today but sliding close to disappearing. In this view, the mammoth is less the true goal than a dramatic test of methods that might one day protect living elephants, rhinos, and countless smaller creatures.

Critics, however, raise hard questions. The money and effort, they warn, might be far better spent protecting the thousands of species now sliding toward extinction. There are worries, too, about releasing a half-ancient creature into a world that has changed completely since it vanished. Even among scientists who admire the science, many quietly wonder whether bringing back the dead is real wisdom or simply human pride. For now, no mammoth walks the earth, and the debate is far from settled. Whatever the final answer turns out to be, the simple fact that the question can now be seriously asked shows how far, and how fast, our power over life itself has grown.
day_materials.translation_zh: 自有人類以來，滅絕一直是單向門：某物種最後一員死去，就永遠消失，只留在骨骸、舊畫與故事裡。如今一小群科學家相信這古老規則或許終能被打破——用基因學新進展讓消失的動物復活，即大膽且具爭議的『去滅絕』。最知名目標是長毛象，這種巨大多毛的象親戚數千年前消失。科學家從北方凍體取得長毛象 DNA 片段，與其現存最近親亞洲象比對，設法編輯象細胞使其帶有長毛象關鍵特徵（濃密長毛、耐極寒），成果不會是完美長毛象，而是能活在凍原的象。支持者說去滅絕能帶來好處：把類長毛象放回北方草原甚至可能藉維持凍土健康而減緩氣候變遷，相關研究也推進了拯救瀕危現存物種的工具。但批評者提出難題：這些錢與心力或許更該用來保護正走向滅絕的數千物種，也擔憂把半古老生物放進已全然改變的世界。連讚賞此科學的人也在想：讓死者復生是智慧，還是人類的傲慢？

day_materials.title: 閱讀測驗二：The Value of Boredom（第 39–42 題）
day_materials.content:
In a world of endless entertainment, boredom has become something we try very hard to avoid. The moment a line slows down or a bus runs late, most of us reach for a phone to fill the empty minutes. Boredom feels unpleasant, even useless, and modern life offers a thousand quick ways to escape it. Yet a number of psychologists now argue that we may be quietly losing something valuable when we never once allow ourselves to be bored. The simple skill of sitting calmly with an empty moment, they warn, is one that a great many of us are slowly forgetting.

Their research suggests that boredom is not simply empty, wasted time. When the mind is unoccupied and a little restless, it tends to wander, drifting freely from one loose thought to another. This wandering is exactly the mental state in which many people come up with fresh ideas and unexpected solutions. Some of history’s famous discoveries and stories are said to have arrived not during busy hours of work, but in dull moments—on a slow train, in a warm bath, or while staring out of a rain-streaked window.

Boredom may also help us understand ourselves a little better. Without a bright screen to grab our attention, we are left alone with our own thoughts, and questions we have been quietly avoiding slowly rise to the surface. Uncomfortable as this can be, it is often exactly how people notice what they truly want, or realise that something in their life needs to change. A dull afternoon, in this sense, can act like a quiet mirror, showing us the very thoughts that the noise of a busy day usually hides.

None of this means that boredom is always pleasant, or that every dull afternoon leads straight to genius. The point is gentler than that. When we reach for a screen at the very first hint of emptiness, we may be trading away quiet moments in which the mind could rest, wander, and surprise us. Sometimes, the researchers gently suggest, the most useful thing we can possibly do is nothing at all. Such advice is hard to follow in a world carefully designed to keep us endlessly and comfortably distracted, yet it may be more valuable now than it has ever been before.
day_materials.translation_zh: 在娛樂無盡的世界，無聊成了我們拚命避免的東西：隊伍一慢、公車一晚，多數人就掏手機填滿空檔。無聊令人不適、甚至看似無用，現代生活也提供千百種逃離之道。但不少心理學家主張，若從不讓自己無聊，我們或許正悄悄失去珍貴之物。研究顯示無聊並非全然空耗：當心智無所事事又有點焦躁，它會漫遊，從一個念頭飄向另一個，而這正是許多人想出新點子與意外解法的狀態。歷史上一些著名發現與故事，據說並非在忙碌工作時、而是在乏味片刻降臨——慢車上、熱水澡中、望著被雨打濕的窗。無聊也幫我們更了解自己：沒有亮螢幕搶注意力，我們獨對己思，一直逃避的問題慢慢浮現；雖不舒服，卻常是人們看清真正想要什麼、或意識到生活該改變的時刻。這不表示無聊總愉快、或每個乏味午後都通向天才；重點更溫和：一有空虛就抓螢幕，可能換走了讓心智休息、漫遊並帶來驚喜的安靜時刻。

question_slots.stem: 【閱讀二】In the final paragraph, the writer says such advice is hard to follow in a world designed to keep us distracted, ______ it may be more valuable now than it has ever been before. Which choice best fits the passage?

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem: 【閱讀二】According to the passage, which of the following are described as possible benefits of allowing ourselves to be bored? (Choose ALL that apply.)

day_materials.title: 綜合測驗短文：Losing the Night Sky（克漏字，空格 {{11}}–{{15}}）
day_materials.content:
On a clear night far from any city, the sky overhead can hold several thousand stars, along with the faint glowing band of the Milky Way. Yet most people alive today have never once seen such a sight. As towns and cities have grown, their lights have spread upward into the night, and this brightness has slowly {{11}} the stars from view. The problem even has its own name: light pollution.

Unlike many other kinds of pollution, this one is surprisingly easy to picture. Streetlamps, glowing signs, and bright floodlights send much of their light uselessly up into the sky, where it scatters and creates a dull orange glow above every large city. {{12}}, a whole generation is now growing up that may reach adulthood without ever seeing more than a handful of the brightest stars.

The effects reach well beyond a lost view. Many animals depend on natural darkness: newly hatched sea turtles can be {{13}} by bright beaches and crawl the wrong way, while migrating birds grow confused by lit-up towers. Even human sleep can suffer when the night is never truly dark.

The good news is that light pollution is one of the few environmental problems that can be {{14}} almost instantly. Shading lamps to point downward, and switching off signs that no one is watching, can bring the stars back within a single night. A number of towns have already done exactly this, proving that a darker sky is a goal still within our {{15}}.
day_materials.translation_zh: 在遠離城市的晴夜，頭頂可有數千顆可見星星與淡淡發光的銀河。但今天多數人從沒見過這景象：城鎮擴張，燈光向夜空蔓延，這片亮光慢慢把星星『遮蔽(hidden)』於視線之外，這問題常見到有了名字——光害。與許多污染不同，它極易想像：路燈、招牌、投射燈把大量光無謂射向天空，散射成每座大城上方的橙色暗光。『結果(As a result)』一整個世代長大成人，可能從沒見過幾顆最亮以外的星。影響不只是失去美景：剛孵化的海龜會被明亮沙灘『誤導(misled)』而爬錯方向，遷徙鳥類被發亮高樓弄糊塗，連人類睡眠在夜不夠黑時也受影響。好消息是，光害是極少數幾乎能『立即解決(solved)』的環境問題：把燈罩住朝下、關掉沒人看的招牌，一夜之間就能讓星星回來。已有城鎮這麼做，證明更暗更豐富的星空仍在我們能力所及(reach)之內。

day_materials.title:
文意選填短文：The Psychology of Colour（空格 {{21}}–{{25}}；詞庫見下）
詞庫 Word Bank：(A) influence  (B) energetic  (C) ignore  (D) depends  (E) persuade  (F) calm  (G) increases  (H) memory　※每格填一字、字不重複，字庫中有 3 字不會用到。
day_materials.content:
Colour is one of the very first things we notice about the world, and it quietly shapes our feelings far more than we usually realise. Long before we read a single word on a package or a poster, its colours have already begun to {{21}} how we feel about what we are looking at. This is exactly why designers, shopkeepers, and advertisers study colour with such great care. The choices they make are rarely accidents; almost every shade on a shelf has been picked for a definite reason.

Warm colours such as red and orange tend to feel {{22}} and exciting. Restaurants often use them because they are believed to catch the eye and even increase appetite. Red is also the colour of warning signs and sale tags, chosen precisely because it is so very hard to {{23}}. Cool colours, by contrast, usually feel calm and trustworthy. Banks and hospitals frequently choose soft blue, hoping their customers will feel safe and relaxed.

Yet the meaning of a colour is not fixed; much of it {{24}} on culture and personal experience. White, for example, stands for purity and weddings in many Western countries, but is closely linked with mourning and funerals in parts of Asia. A colour that feels cheerful to one person may quietly carry sad memories for another. Because of this, clever designers never rely on colour alone; they test their ideas on real people, watching how different shades change the way a product is judged in just a few short seconds.

Understanding these effects gives ordinary people a kind of quiet power. Once we notice how a bright red button or a soft blue wall is gently trying to {{25}} us, we can pause, think clearly, and make our own choices, instead of being quietly pushed along by colours we never even stopped to see. In a world crowded with bright signs all competing for our attention, that small act of noticing turns out to be a surprisingly useful skill.
day_materials.translation_zh: 顏色是我們對世界最先注意到的事物之一，它悄悄左右情緒的程度遠超我們所想。早在讀到包裝或海報上任何一個字之前，色彩已開始『影響(influence)』我們對所見之物的感受，這正是設計師、店家與廣告商如此用心研究顏色的原因。紅、橙等暖色多讓人覺得『有活力(energetic)』又興奮，餐廳常用它們以吸睛、甚至增進食慾；紅色也是警示與特價標籤的顏色，正因它極難『忽視(ignore)』。相對地，冷色多讓人覺得平靜可信，銀行與醫院常選柔和藍色。但顏色的意義並非固定，多半『取決(depends)』於文化與個人經驗：白色在許多西方國家代表純潔與婚禮，在亞洲部分地區卻與哀悼喪禮相連。理解這些效果給了一般人一種安靜的力量：一旦察覺紅色按鈕或藍色牆面正試圖『說服(persuade)』我們，就能停下來、想清楚、自己做選擇。

day_materials.title: 篇章結構短文：How the Potato Changed Europe（挖去 {{31}}、{{32}} 兩句，由選項句庫還原）
day_materials.content:
When we picture the great turning points of human history, we tend to imagine wars, kings, and grand inventions. We rarely stop to think of a humble, lumpy vegetable growing quietly under the cold soil. {{31}} Yet few things have reshaped the continent of Europe as deeply as the potato, a plant that most Europeans had never even seen five hundred years ago.

The potato came originally from the high mountains of South America, where local people had grown and eaten it for thousands of years. When European ships first carried it back across the ocean, however, it was met with deep suspicion. Many farmers flatly refused to plant it, convinced that such a strange, dirt-covered root must be unhealthy or even poisonous. For years, the potato was treated as food fit only for animals and the very poorest people. In some countries, official orders were needed simply to persuade suspicious farmers to give the new crop a fair chance.

Attitudes changed only slowly, often thanks to determined rulers who could clearly see the plant’s promise. {{32}} A single field of potatoes could feed far more people than the same field planted with wheat, and the hardy crop survived in poor soil and cold weather that would have ruined other harvests. As ordinary families began to plant it, hunger became less common, populations grew quickly, and the crowded cities of the modern age slowly became possible. Whole regions that had once known regular famine gradually became able to feed themselves. The change was so great that historians still argue today about just how much of Europe’s later growth this single plant made possible.

Today the potato is so utterly ordinary that we forget how revolutionary it once was. The next time you eat a plate of fries, it is worth remembering that this simple food, once feared and despised, quietly helped to feed a whole continent and change the very course of its history. It is a useful reminder that history is shaped not only by the famous and the powerful, but sometimes by the most ordinary things on our plates.

day_materials.title: 閱讀測驗一：Meat Grown Without Animals（第 35–38 題）
day_materials.content:
For thousands of years, eating meat has meant raising and then killing animals. Today, a small but fast-growing group of scientists and companies is trying to change that ancient equation. In clean laboratories and small factories, they are learning to grow real meat directly from animal cells, without raising or slaughtering any animal at all. The product goes by several names—cultured meat, lab-grown meat, or cell-based meat—but the basic idea behind all of them is the same.

The process begins with a tiny sample of cells taken painlessly from a living animal. These cells are then placed in large steel tanks and fed a careful mixture of nutrients, where they multiply and slowly form muscle, the very same tissue that makes up an ordinary piece of meat. Because the result is genuine animal tissue, supporters argue, it should taste and cook just like the meat we already know, unlike the plant-based imitations sold in shops today. The finished product is not a clever substitute pretending to be meat; chemically speaking, it simply is meat.

The possible benefits are large. Raising animals for food uses enormous amounts of land, water, and grain, and produces a great deal of the gas that warms the planet. Growing meat in tanks could, in theory, use far fewer of these resources and spare billions of animals from crowded farms. For a hungry and warming world, that is a powerful promise. Some supporters also point to safety, arguing that meat grown in clean tanks could carry fewer of the dangerous bacteria sometimes found on ordinary farms.

Serious challenges remain, however. Cultured meat is still extremely expensive to produce, and no one has yet made it cheaply enough to fill an ordinary supermarket shelf. Some people are also uneasy about the very idea of eating meat grown in a factory, and the rules for selling it are still being written in most countries. Winning the public’s trust, many experts believe, may in the end prove even harder than solving the science. Whether cultured meat becomes an everyday food or remains a costly curiosity, its inventors say, may be decided within the next ten years.
day_materials.translation_zh: 數千年來，吃肉意味著飼養再宰殺動物。如今一小群快速成長的科學家與公司想改變這古老等式：在潔淨實驗室與小型工廠，他們學會直接用動物細胞培養真正的肉，完全不飼養或屠宰動物。這產品有多個名字——培養肉、實驗室肉、細胞肉——但核心概念相同。過程始於從活體動物無痛採取的一小撮細胞，置入大型鋼槽、餵以養分混合液，細胞增殖並慢慢形成肌肉，即一般肉的組織。支持者說，因為它是真正的動物組織，理應和我們熟悉的肉一樣好吃好煮，不像市售植物仿肉；成品不是假裝成肉的替代品，化學上它就是肉。可能的好處很大：養殖耗費大量土地、水、穀物並排放暖化氣體，槽中培養理論上能省下許多資源、讓數十億動物免於擁擠農場，對飢餓又暖化的世界是有力承諾。但挑戰仍在：培養肉造價極高，尚無法便宜到擺上一般超市貨架，有些人也對『工廠養的肉』心存不安。

day_materials.title: 閱讀測驗二：The Secret Network of the Forest（第 39–42 題）
day_materials.content:
To walk through a forest is to walk among what looks like a crowd of separate, silent trees, each one standing alone and competing with its neighbours for light and water. For a very long time, this is more or less exactly how scientists pictured a forest. In recent decades, however, a series of surprising discoveries has begun to tell a very different story—one in which the trees are quietly connected and share far more than anyone had ever imagined.

The connection lies hidden underground. The roots of most trees are wrapped in extremely fine threads of fungus, far too thin to notice, which spread through the soil and link one tree to another. Through this vast underground network, sometimes nicknamed the ‘wood wide web,’ trees can actually pass sugar, water, and chemical signals back and forth. A large, healthy tree, for instance, may send spare food through the fungi to a smaller, shaded seedling that cannot yet make enough of its own. In some cases the fungi even carry food from a tree of one species to a tree of another, quietly blurring the line between competitor and partner.

Even more remarkably, the network seems to carry warnings. When insects begin to attack one tree, it can send chemical signals through the fungi and the air, and nearby trees, receiving the message, start to prepare their own chemical defences before the insects even arrive. The fungi are not doing this for free, of course; in return for moving food and messages, they receive sugars from the trees, in one of nature’s oldest partnerships. In this way, a forest behaves less like a group of strangers and more like a single, cooperating community.

These findings are slowly changing how people think about forests, and about nature itself. A forest, it turns out, is not simply a collection of individuals struggling alone, but a web of quiet partnerships built up patiently over many centuries. When a single old tree is cut down, we may be losing far more than its wood; we may be cutting a living thread that once helped an entire forest survive. Protecting a forest, seen this way, means protecting not just the trees we can see, but the hidden web that ties them all together.
day_materials.translation_zh: 走過森林，看似走在一群各自獨立、彼此為光和水競爭的沉默樹木之間；長久以來科學家大致就這麼看森林。但近數十年一連串驚奇發現開始訴說截然不同的故事——樹木其實悄悄相連、分享的遠比想像多。連結藏在地下：多數樹的根被極細、細到看不見的真菌絲包覆，穿過土壤把一棵樹連到另一棵。透過這被暱稱『樹聯網(wood wide web)』的地下網路，樹木能來回傳送糖、水與化學訊號：一棵高大健康的樹可透過真菌把多餘養分送給還無法自製足夠養分、被遮蔭的小苗，有時真菌甚至把養分從一個樹種送到另一個樹種，模糊了競爭者與夥伴的界線。更驚人的是這網路似乎會傳警訊：當昆蟲開始啃食一棵樹，它能透過真菌與空氣送出化學訊號，鄰近樹木收到便在昆蟲到來前先備好化學防禦。真菌當然不是白做工——牠們以搬運養分與訊息換取樹木的糖分，是自然界最古老的夥伴關係之一。

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem: 【閱讀二】根據文章第二段，作者描述樹根與真菌的關係：「The roots of most trees ______ in extremely fine threads of fungus, far too thin to notice.」依原文語態與時態，空格應填入下列何者？
question_slots.explanation: 【題幹中譯】依原文語態與時態，空格應填入哪一個？【線索句】原文：「The roots of most trees are wrapped in extremely fine threads of fungus」（多數樹的根被極細的真菌絲包覆）。【正解B】主詞 The roots 是「被」真菌絲包覆的受詞，且全文陳述普遍事實用現在式，故用現在式被動語態 are wrapped。【辨析】(A) wrap 為主動現在式，語意變成「樹根去包覆真菌」與原意相反；(C) wrapping 為分詞，無法單獨當述語動詞，句子缺主要動詞；(D) have wrapped 為主動完成式，語態錯誤；(E) were wrapping 為過去進行主動，時態與語態皆不合，全文以現在式描述普遍事實。【評析】語態與時態辨析題，關鍵在辨識主詞為動作承受者（被動）＋普遍事實（現在式）；屬中等文法題。

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem: 【閱讀二】文章第三段提到真菌搬運養分與訊息並非無償：「The fungi are not doing this for free, of course; ______ moving food and messages, they receive sugars from the trees.」依原文語意與詞性，空格應填入下列何者？
question_slots.explanation: 【題幹中譯】依原文語意與詞性，空格應填入哪一個？【線索句】原文：「in return for moving food and messages, they receive sugars from the trees」（真菌以搬運養分與訊息換取樹木的糖分）。【正解B】in return for「以…作為回報／交換」正好表達真菌搬運養分訊息、樹木回饋糖分的互利交換，且後接動名詞 moving，詞性相符。【辨析】(A) instead of「而非、取代」語意相反；(C) regardless of「不管、無視」不合互利語境；(D) in spite of「儘管、雖然」表讓步，與交換關係不符；(E) as well as「以及」為對等連接，無法表達「作為回報」的交換關係。【評析】連接詞／片語語意與詞性辨析題，須抓「互利交換」語境並確認後接動名詞；屬中等題。

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem: 【閱讀二】根據文章第二段，樹木可以透過地下真菌網路（'wood wide web'）在彼此之間傳送哪些東西？下列選項中，何者屬於原文明確提到能透過此網路來回傳遞的項目？（本題為多選題，請選出全部三個正確選項）
question_slots.explanation: 【題幹中譯】樹木可透過地下真菌網路來回傳遞哪些項目？（多選，選出全部三個正確項）【線索句】原文：「trees can actually pass sugar, water, and chemical signals back and forth」（樹木能來回傳送糖、水與化學訊號）。【正解A、B、C】糖(sugar)、水(water)、化學訊號(chemical signals)三者原文明列，皆可經真菌網路來回傳遞。【辨析】(D) Sunlight 陽光：原文開頭提樹木為『光』競爭，但陽光並非透過地下網路傳送的項目；(E) Insects 昆蟲：昆蟲是啃食樹木、觸發警訊的攻擊者，並非網路傳送之物。【評析】細節多選題，真項數＝宣告數（3），三個正確項全出自同一線索句，全自動判分；屬中等題。

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem: 【閱讀二】文章第二段提到真菌有時把養分從一個樹種送到另一個樹種，「quietly blurring the line between competitor and partner.」畫線片語 blurring the line 在此最接近下列哪一個意思？

options.text: 明確劃分兩者、使界線更清楚
使兩者之間的界線變得模糊、不再分明
完全切斷兩者之間的任何關係
在兩者之間畫上一條全新的紅線
強迫兩者互相激烈競爭

question_slots.explanation: 【題幹中譯】畫線片語 blurring the line 最接近哪個意思？【線索句】原文：「the fungi even carry food from a tree of one species to a tree of another, quietly blurring the line between competitor and partner」（真菌把養分從一樹種送到另一樹種，悄悄模糊了競爭者與夥伴的界線）。【正解B】blur the line 意為「使界線模糊、不再分明」，因原本被視為競爭者的樹木其實互相供養，故競爭者與夥伴的分界變模糊。【辨析】(A) 與 blur（模糊）語意相反，界線並非更清楚；(C) 「切斷關係」與原文『互相供養』的連結相反；(D) 「畫新紅線」是製造新界線，與模糊界線相反；(E) 「強迫競爭」與本段強調『競爭者其實也是夥伴』的合作意涵相反。【評析】字義／片語推義題，須由上下文（跨物種供養）推得 blur the line＝『使界線模糊』；屬中等題。
question_slots.review_advice: 推論題抓末段『cutting a living thread...helped an entire forest survive』。

question_slots.subject: 英文
question_slots.stem:
【中譯英・手寫】請將下列兩句中文譯成通順、文法正確的英文（每句 4 分，共 8 分）：
1. 儘管失敗了很多次，他從未放棄實現夢想的決心。
2. 這座城市正在興建更多綠地，好讓居民有休閒放鬆的空間。
answer: 1. Although he failed many times, he never gave up his determination to realize his dream.
2. The city is building more green spaces so that residents can have room to relax.
question_slots.explanation: 【評分導向解析】本題兩句各 4 分，逐一比對關鍵結構與詞彙給分。第1句「儘管失敗了很多次，他從未放棄實現夢想的決心」：得分點① 讓步子句 Although/Even though he failed many times；② 主句 he never gave up his determination to realize (fulfill) his dream；「決心」用 determination＋不定詞 to realize，「實現夢想」realize/fulfill his dream。第2句「這座城市正在興建更多綠地，好讓居民有休閒放鬆的空間」：得分點① 現在進行式 The city is building more green spaces；② 目的子句 so that residents can have room/space to relax。【常見扣分】Although 與 but 不可同句連用；so that 後須完整子句且用 can/could；主謂一致與時態（is building）正確；green spaces 用複數。參考譯文：1) Although he failed many times, he never gave up his determination to realize his dream. 2) The city is building more green spaces so that residents can have room to relax.
question_slots.review_advice: 第1句用 Although＋主要子句，注意 give up 後接名詞/動名詞；第2句用 so that 表目的，動詞用現在進行式。
